newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria president opposes ban on ex-communists.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria president opposes ban on ex-communists.

text.p: Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov said on Wednesday he opposed a draft bill before parliament banning former leading communists from holding senior state posts.

"I do not think such a law would have a stimulative effect for Bulgaria, nor would it have a healing effect on the country's society which has embarked on the road to the reforms needed to overcome the crisis," Stoyanov told reporters.

The draft seeks to ban former members of local and central ruling bodies of the Bulgarian Communist Party from holding top positions in the state administration, big state firms and state media within five years from its approval.
Stoyanov said the bill should have been passed right after the collapse of totalitarian rule in November 1989 to achieve the right effect and promote national consensus.
"We are too late now...More than seven years have passed since November 10, (1989), we have already given birth to our national consensus," said Stoyanov.
The draft was introduced in the parliament two weeks ago by the small People's Union, a coalition partner of the ruling Union of Democratic Forces (UDF).
The Socialist Party, formed by leading communists after 1989, said the law violated the constitution and the Socialist daily Duma estimated it would affect 200,000 people.
The UDF, which won elections after the Socialists were toppled in February by month-long street protests, has not yet stated its position on the draft.
Sources at the Presidency told Reuters Stoyanov was determined to veto the bill if parliament approved it.
